title: Common Table Expressions (CTEs) for Multi-Step Aggregations
realWorldScenario: Executive leadership requires a customer spending tiers report: aggregate total spend per customer first, then filter for customers whose lifetime spend exceeds $300.
questionStatement: Write a query using a `WITH` clause (CTE) named `customer_spending` that aggregates `customer_id` and `total_spent` (sum of `total_amount` for orders with status `'DELIVERED'`). In the main query, join with `customers` to return `customers.name`, `customer_spending.total_spent`, ordered by `total_spent` descending.
starterCode:
-- Multi-step aggregation using CTE
WITH customer_spending AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    SUM(total_amount) AS total_spent
  FROM orders
  WHERE status = 'DELIVERED'
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT
  c.name,
  cs.total_spent
FROM customer_spending cs
JOIN customers c ON cs.customer_id = c.id
WHERE cs.total_spent > 300
ORDER BY cs.total_spent DESC;
hints: Define the CTE with WITH customer_spending AS (...)
Select from the CTE and join with customers on customer_id.
